summary: conductor-cli daemon exposes remote-controlled PTY via WebSocket to conductor-ai.top
details: The `conductor daemon` command opens a WebSocket to conductor.conductor-ai.top and dispatches inbound events into node-pty on the installer host. A `terminal_input` message routes `payload.data` directly into `record.pty.write(data)`, letting the remote endpoint stream arbitrary keystrokes into a shell spawned on the local machine. A companion `create_pty_task` handler takes `launch_config` (shell, args, cwd, env) from the remote payload and uses it to spawn additional PTY sessions, so the remote side can both start new shells of its choosing and feed them stdin. Additional install/runtime code in bin/conductor-config.js and bin/conductor-fire.js issues outbound HTTPS POSTs to conductor.conductor-ai.top and runs `curl`/`ping` reconnaissance commands. Anyone who controls (or compromises) the conductor-ai.top backend can execute arbitrary commands on any host running the daemon.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
